When fierce planets are situated in the fourth house from <s>Venus</s>, or when the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (<s>Venus</s>) is in the middle of two fierce ones,
and is not accompanied by or aspected by benefic planets, death of the wife occurs through fire, falling, or noose.
When the <s>Moon</s> and <s>Sun</s> are in the twelfth and sixth houses from the <s>lagna</s>, they declare the birth of one who is one-eyed along with the wife;
when <s>Venus</s> and <s>Sun</s> are in the seventh house, or situated in the ninth and fifth, they declare the one born to have a defective wife.

When the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (<s>Venus</s>) is in a trine at the <s>lagna</s>, at the junction of the seventh and twelfth houses, the husband is barren — unless the fifth house is joined with benefics;
when malefic planets occupy the twelfth, seventh, and first houses, and the <s>Moon</s> is waning, one born is without children and wife — as determined by the wise.
When Venus is in the seventh in the division of Saturn and Mars and aspected by them, if those two are with the Moon, the man is unfaithful with women;
when Venus and Moon are in the seventh, the man is wifeless or without sons; when the mature bodies of man and woman are aspected by benefics, [he becomes] a husband of beautiful women.

A destroyer of his lineage when Moon, <s>Rāhu</s>, and malefics are in the tenth, seventh, and fourth; a craftsman when conjoined with Mercury in a <s>drekkāṇa</s> (decan) aspected by Saturn in an angle;
born of a slave-woman when <s>Rāhu</s> is in the twelfth in Saturn's division; lowly when the Sun and Moon in the seventh are aspected by Saturn.
When Venus and Mars are aspected by malefics in the seventh, [there is] a bodily disease; when the Moon is in a Cancer or Scorpio division conjoined with malefics, a genital disease;

when malefics are in the twelfth and second with leucoderma, the Moon in the ascendant and the Sun in the seventh; when the Moon is in the tenth and Mars is in the seventh, [the person is] crippled, if Saturn is in the second.
When the Moon is between two malefics in Capricorn or Cancer, [the person] suffers from asthma, consumption, splenic disease, abscess, and abdominal tumor;
one wastes away when the Sun and Moon are in each other's sign and division; or when both are in the same [sign], one becomes emaciated.
When the Moon is in the divisions of Aśvinī, the middle [signs], Pisces, Cancer, Capricorn, or Aries, [the person has] leprosy with Saturn and Mars or when aspected by them;
one with leprosy also when Scorpio, Cancer, and Taurus in Capricorn go to the trines, conjoined with or aspected by malefics.
The Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn situated in the eighth, sixth, second, and twelfth respectively —
being strong planets, the causes of defects, they produce blindness in people.
Malefics conjoined in the ninth, eleventh, third, and fifth, and not aspected by benefics,
certainly cause damage to hearing; and in the seventh, they cause dental deformity.
When the Moon rises in Leo, [the person is] possessed by demons when malefics are in the trines;
when the Sun with an eclipsed disc is in the ascendant, [the person is] deprived of eyesight.
Touched by wind [i.e., insane] when <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) with Saturn is in the seventh and the ascendant; maddened when Mars is in the seventh and Jupiter occupies the ascendant;
likewise when Saturn is in the ascendant and Mars is in the ninth and seventh; born to servitude when the waning Moon is in the twelfth, the child of the Sun [Saturn] rising.
When the lords of the sign, division, and the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are in the divisions of debilitation lords or in the sixth,
from few, moderate, or many of these, one should know [the person] to be respectively a voluntary servant, a purchased slave, a born slave, or a hereditary servant.
One with deformed teeth when malefics aspect and the ascendant is Taurus, Aries, or Sagittarius; bald when the ascendant is in a malefic sign, Sagittarius, or Taurus;
when the Sun aspected by malefics is in the ninth or fifth, [the person has] weak eyesight; when Saturn [is there], multiple diseases; when Mars, the man is crippled.
With malefics in the twelfth, fifth, second, and ninth, bondage of the dwelling should be determined according to the corresponding [house];
likewise with <s>drekkāṇas</s> (decans) bearing serpent, chain, and noose, strongly aspected by malefics, [the result is] bondage.
One afflicted by epilepsy and consumption when the Moon with Saturn goes to [the house of] Mars aspected by it, placed in [the sign of] the halo;
a hired servant when the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are in the tenth and the ground [fourth], not aspected by benefics; the previously mentioned [determine whether they are] best, worst, or middling.
Whatever result in a man's horoscope is suitable for women, that should be declared; or everything should be applied to their husbands;
their husband's death [is indicated] by the eighth house; physical appearance by [planets in] the ascendant and Moon; good fortune by the seventh; and the husband likewise.
When the ascendant and Moon are in even signs, the woman is of natural disposition, endowed with good character and ornaments, and when aspected by benefics;
when in odd signs, she is endowed with masculine form and character; and when conjoined with and aspected by malefics, she is devoid of virtues.
A wicked woman goes into servitude; a virtuous woman [appears] deceitful, endowed with bad conduct —
in the sign of Mars and in the divisions of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus in sequence.
Wicked, a remarried woman, virtuous, skilled in arts, and renowned for qualities — [these are the results] in the sign of <s>Rāhu</s>;
she would be deceitful, equal to a eunuch, chaste, and rich in virtues with scattered desires — in Mercury's [sign].
Self-willed, a husband-killer, many-virtued, skilled in crafts, unchaste in the Moon's sign; of manly conduct, an adulteress in the Sun's sign; a queen's bride, approaching forbidden men;

in Jupiter's sign, of single virtue, little passion, supremely virtuous, wise, and chaste; a slave, delighting in the lowly in Saturn's sign; devoted to husband, wicked in progeny — [according to] their respective divisions.
This result is from the <s>triṃśāṃśas</s> (thirtieth divisions) conjoined with the Moon and ascendant;
one should consider what has been stated according to the distinction of strength and weakness of those two.
When Venus and Mars are in the tenth, settled in each other's division, or in Venus's [division], if the division originates from Aquarius,
she brings to peace the fire of passion, poison, and flame [kindled] by women of human form among women.

When the seventh house is empty, [the husband is] a coward; when benefic planets aspect the seventh, [he is] a eunuch; when Mercury and Saturn are in the seventh in a movable sign, [the husband is] always away on travels;
abandoned by the Sun, widowed by Mars when placed in the seventh in youth; when Virgo itself is aspected by malefics and Saturn is in the seventh, she grows old [without a husband].
Widowed with fiery [planets] in the seventh; a remarried woman with mixed [planets]; when a malefic of low strength is in the seventh, rejected by her own husband though aspected by benefics;
when Venus and Mars are in each other's division, the woman is attached to another man; or if those two with the Moon are in the seventh, then with the husband's consent.
When Venus with the Moon is in the ascendant in Saturn's or Mars's sign and aspected by malefics, she is a courtesan together with her mother;
in Mars's division in the seventh aspected by Saturn, [she is] prone to disease; with beautiful hips and beloved when in the division of a benefic planet.
The husband is old and foolish in the sign or division of Saturn; lustful toward women and wrathful in Mars's [sign or division];
in Venus's, the husband is handsome, exceedingly fortunate; in Mercury's, the husband is learned and skilled.
Subject to passion and gentle in the Moon's [sign or division]; in Jupiter's, the husband is virtuous and has conquered his senses;
and one who performs exceedingly gentle love-making in Saturn's — [this is the result] in the house or division of the seventh.
Jealous and devoted to comfort when the Moon and Venus are in the ascendant; skilled in arts, happy, and rich in virtues when Mercury and Moon [are there];
with Venus and Mercury, she is beautiful, fortunate, and knowledgeable in arts; when all three benefics [are in the ascendant], she has manifold wealth, happiness, and virtues.
When a malefic is in the eighth, widowhood [is indicated]; the age at which widowhood is declared equals the age [corresponding to] the sign in which the lord of the eighth is situated;
when benefics are in their own places, death comes to her by itself; when the Moon is in Virgo, Scorpio, or Leo, [there is] having few sons.
When Saturn has moderate strength, and Moon, Venus, and Mercury are devoid of strength, with the remaining [planets] endowed with vigor, she is harsh; if the ascendant is an odd sign,
when Jupiter, Mars, the ascendant, and Moon are strong, with the ascendant sign being even, the woman is renowned on earth, skilled in many <s>śāstras</s>, and speaks of <s>Brahman</s>.
When a malefic is in the seventh, the young woman without doubt takes up renunciation equal to that of the planet in the ninth;
at the time of marriage, the ceremony of choice, the giving away, and even in deliberation — all this should be applied.

Death [is determined] by the strong [planets] aspecting the eighth house; arising from the humor of that [planet]; [affecting] the body part of the sign conjoined with it; manifold when many planets are endowed with strength;

caused by fire, water, and weapons; produced by fever and disease; caused by thirst and hunger — in the eighth, [indicated] by the Sun and so forth; in [signs] movable and so forth, [death occurs] in another's [land], one's own, or on the road.
Death by falling from a mountain top when Sun and Mars are in the tenth and fourth; in a well when Saturn, Moon, and Mars are in the fourth, seventh, and tenth;
in Virgo, [death is] from one's own people; when Sun and Moon are aspected by malefic planets, if both are in each other's ascendant, then [death by] drowning in water.

When Saturn is in Cancer, death from abdominal water disease (dropsy); in Capricorn, from [an attack by] a deer; originating from weapons and fire when the Moon is between two malefics in Mars's sign;
in Virgo, death caused by blood-born wasting; likewise when the Moon is in Saturn's sign — if so, death by rope, fire, and falls.

From bondage when the ninth [house lord] from the fourth [is placed with] those two malefics, aspected by a benefic planet; and with <s>drekkāṇas</s> (decans) bearing noose, serpent, and chains in the eighth, [death is] from bondage;
in Virgo, when the Moon goes to the seventh accompanied by a malefic, and Venus is in Aries, and the Sun is in the ascendant — know [this to be] death caused by a woman, at home.
Body pierced by a spike when Mars is in the fourth and the Sun also in the tenth, with Saturn;
with the Sun in the fourth and Mars in the sky (tenth), aspected by the waning Moon — death by being struck with wood, when aspected by Saturn.
The body struck by a club on [the part corresponding to] the eighth, second, and fourth [houses], by Mars, Saturn, and the Sun conjoined with the waning Moon;
by those same [planets] in the tenth, ninth, ascendant, and fifth — death by smoke, fire, bondage, and bodily beating.
With Mars, Sun, and Saturn in the fourth, seventh, and tenth, death [comes] from weapons, fire, and the wrath of the king;
with Saturn, Moon, and Mars in their own and the fourth houses, bodily destruction should be known as caused by wounds, worms, and so forth.
When the Sun is in the tenth and Mars in the fourth (nadir), death by a fall from a vehicle; caused by machine-crushing when Mars is in the seventh and Saturn and Moon in the ascendant;
amidst excrement when Mars, Saturn, and Moon are in Libra, Aries, and Saturn's sign; or when the declining Moon, Sun, and Mars are in the tenth, seventh, and fourth houses.
When the waning Moon in the eighth is aspected by Mars endowed with strength and Saturn,
death may be from disease arising in the private parts, caused by worms, weapons, or burning.
When the Sun is in the seventh with Mars, Saturn is in the eighth, the waning Moon has gone to the nadir — [death occurs] among birds (in the sky);
with Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Moon in the ascendant, fifth, eighth, and ninth — death by [falling from] mountain peaks, lightning, and wall-collapses.
The twenty-second <s>drekkāṇa</s> (decan) is declared by the sages as the cause of death;
its lord or the [lord of the] eighth house gives death according to its own qualities.
This should be determined from the <s>horā</s>, <s>navāṃśa</s> lord, and [planets of] equal ground, through yoga, aspect, and so forth;
delusion at the time of death equals the unrisen portion; when aspected by its own lord, it is doubled; by benefics, tripled.
Mixed with fire and water — ash, moisture, and desiccation; [from] serpent groups situated in the house of death, [the body] ends in excrement;
thus the transformation of the corpse should be contemplated as stated; from the treatise composed by <s>Pṛthu</s>, the destination and post-mortem state should be considered.

<s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), the Moon, and Venus [lead to] divine [realms]; the Sun and Mars to the realm of the ancestors; Saturn and Mercury to animal [births]; and [all malefics together] produce hellish [births];
from the lord of the <s>drekkāṇa</s> presided over by the strength of the Sun and Moon — superior, middling, and inferior [destinies] from exaltation and depression in the post-mortem state.
The destination also [comes from] the lord of the <s>drekkāṇa</s> of the sixth and eighth when the seventh is occupied; or when Jupiter, in the sixth, angle, or eighth, is in its own exaltation,
rising in the last house in a benefic portion, <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) occurs; if [the planets] are cast aside by strength, the remainder [determines the fate].
At the time when the conception and birth are not known, one should declare the birth from the ascendant of the questioner;
in the first or second half of the [rising] sign, one should find the birth when the Sun is in the northern or southern [course].
With Jupiter in the trines of the ascendant, the years should be estimated in three portions from inference of age;
summer [is indicated] when the Sun is in the ascendant; the other seasons from the other [planets]; the <s>ayana</s> (solstice) and <s>ṛtu</s> (season) from the Sun's course.
Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are to be interchanged with Venus, Mars, and Saturn in the reversed <s>ayana</s>;
in the first portion of the <s>drekkāṇa</s>, [it is] the first month; and the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) should be estimated proportionally.
Here too, the experts skilled in <s>horā</s> (horoscopy), the best among the twice-born, point to the <s>tithi</s> equal to the Sun's degree;
in [signs] designated as night and day, the birth [time] should be estimated in reverse order, and the hours from the degrees in sequence.
Some declare the month named after the bright [fortnight's] end from the <s>navāṃśas</s> occupied by the Moon.
the <s>lagna</s>, trine, and highest strength are declared through the limbs, ornaments, and such indicators.
As far as the <s>Moon</s> has gone from the <s>lagna</s>, one should predict the birth sign at that distance from the <s>Moon</s>;
when <s>Pisces</s> rises, a pair of fish is indicated — it should be considered through the appearance, food brought, form, and sounds.
The <s>lagna</s> resembling the <s>Horā</s> and <s>Navāṃśa</s>, and in whichever <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> the <s>Sun</s> is from the <s>lagna</s>,
from that one should predict the <s>lagna</s> at that position — thus the <s>śāstra</s> (science) declares for the birth of the questioner.
One should predict the birth when a powerful planet occupies the <s>lagna</s>; the remainder when the shadow in <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) is multiplied;
one should predict the form as seated, sleeping, rising, or standing, and the <s>lagna</s> as being in the wife, happiness, command, or rising house.

<s>Taurus</s>-<s>Leo</s>, <s>Gemini</s>-<s>Scorpio</s>, <s>Aries</s>-<s>Libra</s>, <s>Virgo</s>-<s>Capricorn</s> — in the <s>saṃvarga</s> (combination) method with values of ten, eight, and seven; the rest are multiplied by their own numbers;

<s>Jupiter</s>, <s>Mars</s>, <s>Libra</s>, and the <s>Moon's</s> signs follow the first pattern; the remaining planets follow <s>Mercury's</s> pattern — this is the fixed rule for signs, and the <s>varga</s> classification should be made with the planetary conjunctions.
The remainder when multiplied by seven and divided by the cube of three gives the sign; then by subtracting nine, or not, or from that,
thus from the wife, brother, son, and enemy signs, one should predict those of the questioner through the rising sign.
Years, seasons, months, <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), day and night are the <s>nakṣatras</s>; at the time of the <s>velā</s> (moment) rising, sign, <s>Navāṃśa</s> divisions should be made;
further multiplied by ten and so forth, divided by their own divisions, through the <s>Navāṃśa</s> giving and subtracting, the years and other periods are obtained.
In groups of ten, one should know the years, seasons, and months likewise;
in groups of eight also, half-months from a month, and <s>tithis</s> are similarly declared.
Day, night, and the birth, as well as the <s>nakṣatra</s> determination,
in groups of seven also, one should always observe the <s>vargas</s> (divisions).
The <s>velā</s> (time), <s>lagna</s>, <s>Horā</s>, and <s>Navāṃśa</s>,
in groups of five one should know — for the determination of a lost horoscope.
The syllables of the initiation-name, doubled, combined with the shadow in <s>aṅgulas</s>,
the remainder divided by three and nine gives the <s>nakṣatra</s>, beginning from <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>.
Two, three, four, fourteen, ten, seven, seven multiplied by three, nine, and eight — beginning from <s>Indra</s>;
multiplied by five and ten, with the directional face added, the <s>nakṣatra</s> beginning from <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>.
Thus this method of lost horoscopy (<s>naṣṭa-jātaka</s>) has been explained by me in many ways;
therefore, good students should accept it after testing through instruments, as it truly is.
A dark man with a white cloth wrapped around his waist, as if capable of protecting,
fierce, holding an upraised axe, with red eyes — this is the form of the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Aries</s>, as taught by the <s>Yavanas</s> (Greeks).
A woman with red garments, ornaments, craving food, pot-shaped, horse-faced, and afflicted with thirst,
standing on one foot — this is the <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> form in the middle of <s>Aries</s>, as taught by the <s>Yavanas</s>.
Cruel, skilled in arts, tawny-haired, desirous of action, with broken vows, having lifted that egg in hand,
wearing red garments, fierce — the third <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Aries</s> is thus described.
A woman with curly, cropped hair, a pot-like body, wearing burnt cloth, her mind set on food and thirst,
desiring ornaments — this is the form of the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Taurus</s>.
One who knows fields, grain, houses, cows, and arts, skilled with the plow and cart,
carrying a load on the shoulder equal to a bull-lord, absorbed in hunger, goat-faced, wearing dirty clothes —
having an elephant-like body, white tusks, feet like a <s>śarabha</s> (mythical beast), a tawny form,
with a mind agitated by greed for sheep and deer — this one is at the edge of the forest of <s>Taurus</s>.
A woman desiring work involving needles, endowed with beauty, respectful of ornament-making,
of few offspring, with raised arms, in her fertile season — the experts declare this the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of the third sign (<s>Gemini</s>).
Standing in a garden, armored, bearing a bow, brave, weapon-bearing, with a face like <s>Garuḍa</s>,
thinking about play, children, and ornamental purposes — this is in the middle of the sign <s>Gemini</s>.
Adorned like <s>Varuṇa</s>, with many gems, with bound quiver, armor, and bow,
learned in the arts of dance and music, a poet — at the end of the sign <s>Gemini</s>.
Bearing leaves, roots, and fruits, with an elephant-like body, dwelling in a sandalwood forest, with <s>śarabha</s>-like feet,
with a face like a boar, a horse's neck — they declare this the first form of <s>Cancer</s>.
A woman crowned with lotuses, bearing a serpent on her head, in the terrible forest, crying out,
having taken refuge on a branch of a <s>palāśa</s> tree — she stands in the middle of the sign <s>Cancer</s>.
For the sake of the wife's ornaments, one in a boat goes to the ocean, entwined by serpents,
and adorned with golden ornaments, flat-faced — this one is in the last part of <s>Cancer</s>.
On top of a <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) tree, a vulture and a jackal; a dog and a man wearing dirty garments,
crying out, separated from mother and father — this is declared to be the first form of <s>Leo</s>.
A horse-shaped man with a white garland on his head, wearing a black deerskin blanket,
unapproachable like a lion, bearing a drawn bow, with a curved nose — this is the middle <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Leo</s>.
Bear-faced, with monkey-like movements, bearing a staff, fruit, and meat,
a bearded man with curly hair — this is the last <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Leo</s>.
A maiden with a pot full of flowers, her body covered with soiled garments,
desiring the union of cloth and wealth, wishing for the family of the teacher — this is the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Virgo</s>.
A man holding a pen, dark-complexioned, with cloth and veins visible, engaged in exercise,
bearing a large bow, with body covered in hair — this is the middle <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s>.
A fair woman protected by a well-washed fine silk garment, tall, with a pot and a bracelet in hand,
a devout woman proceeding to a temple — they declare this the last <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Virgo</s>.
A man in the interior of a market-street, holding a balance, skilled in weighing and measuring, with a standard weight in hand,
thinking about merchandise and its price — the <s>Yavanas</s> declare this the first form of <s>Libra</s>.
Holding a pot, a vulture-faced man desires to fly forth;
hungry and thirsty, his mind on wife and children — this is the middle <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Libra</s>.
Standing and terrifying, adorned with gems, in the forest, bearing a golden quiver and armor, frightening the animals,
a man with a monkey's form, bearing fruit and meat — this is declared by the <s>Yavanas</s> as the end of <s>Libra</s>.
A woman without clothes and ornaments, coming ashore from the great ocean,
displaced from her station, her feet bound by serpents, beautiful — this is the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Scorpio</s>.
A woman desiring the comforts of a dwelling, her body entwined by serpents for the sake of the season,
with a body like a tortoise and a pot — they declare this the middle form of <s>Scorpio</s>.
Broad, flat, tortoise-like, and crooked, terrifying dogs, deer, boars, and jackals,
and guarding the region of the sandalwood mountain — this is the lord of the last part of <s>Scorpio</s>.
A man with a human torso, a horse-like body, holding a drawn bow, stationed at a hermitage,
guarding the ritual implements and ascetics — this is the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Sagittarius</s>.
A beautiful woman of <s>campaka</s>-gold complexion, seated on an auspicious seat — the middle form,
handling ocean gems — this is declared the middle <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Sagittarius</s>.
A bearded man of golden <s>campaka</s> color, seated on an excellent seat, holding a staff,
carrying silk garments and a deerskin — this is the third form of the ninth sign.
Hairy, with crocodile-like tusks, a body like a pig of iron,
bearing bonds, nets, and fetters, with a fierce face — this is the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Capricorn</s>.
A woman skilled in the arts, with eyes elongated like lotus petals, dark, seeking colorful things,
with ears adorned with iron ornaments — a woman is declared for the middle of <s>Capricorn</s>.
With a body like a <s>Kinnara</s>, wearing a blanket, equipped with quiver, bow, and armor,
carrying a gem-studded pot on the shoulder — this is the last <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Capricorn</s>.
With a mind agitated by oils, liquor, water, food, and income, wearing a blanket,
dressed in silk-cocoon garments and deerskin, with a vulture-like face — this is the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Aquarius</s>.
Near a burnt cart and a <s>śālmali</s> tree, a woman in the forest carries metals,
covered with a dirty cloth, with vessels on the head — this is the middle <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s>.
Dark, with hairy ears, wearing a crown, bearing bark, leaves, resin, and fruits,
carrying vessels mixed with metals — this one is at the end of <s>Aquarius</s>.
With hands full of ladles, vessels, pearls, gems, and conch shells,
adorned, sailing by boat across the ocean for the sake of the wife's ornaments — this is the first <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Pisces</s>.
A woman with retinue approaches a boat with very tall flags and banners, coming to the shore of the ocean;
with a <s>campaka</s>-colored face — the sages declare this the second <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Pisces</s>.
Near a pit, with body entwined by serpents, a man without clothes in the wilderness,
his inner self agitated by thieves and fire, crying out — this is the last <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> of <s>Pisces</s>.
The division of signs, the distinction of planetary origins, non-human birth, then the time of conception,
then birth, then immediate death, then longevity, the ripening of <s>daśā</s> (planetary periods), and what is called <s>Aṣṭakavarga</s>,
livelihood, royal combinations, celestial combinations, lunar combinations and the combinations beginning with bodily constitution,
renunciation, then sign-character, aspect, houses, then support combinations, and miscellaneous topics,
inauspicious combinations, the horoscopy of women, death, then inauspicious birth, and the <s>Dreṣkāṇa</s> —
twenty-five chapters make up the birth section; I shall now also describe the travel section (<s>yātrika</s>).
Questions, <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), <s>nakṣatra</s>, day, and moment, the <s>Moon</s>, the <s>lagna</s>, and then the classification of <s>lagnas</s>,
the purification of planets, and then the bow-discussion, what is called <s>vimiśraka</s> (mixed), and bodily trembling,
thereafter the worship of <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret beings), then dreams, then the method of bathing is declared,
the sacrifice of planets, and then departure, and the teaching of omens in order,
the time of marriage, the calculation of planets — each described separately — and then the extensive branch;
this compendium of <s>jyotiṣa</s> (astrology) in three divisions has been made by me for the benefit of those versed in divination.
This entire <s>śāstra</s> was composed extensively by others; following that, this brief version has been made by me for the purpose of indicating that subject alone;
whatever has been said here that is capable, if my intelligence is insufficient — may that be forgiven by the good people.
Whatever destruction befalls this text as it circulates, through the gradual process of being transmitted through many mouths,
or whatever little has been badly done or left undone by me — a learned person should attend to that, setting aside partiality.
The son of <s>Ādityadāsa</s>, having obtained knowledge from him, at <s>Kāpitthaka</s>, having received the gracious boon of the <s>Sun</s>,
<s>Varāhamihira</s> of <s>Avanti</s>, having duly examined the opinions of the sages, made this fierce yet beautiful work.
With a mind that has obtained grace through prostration at the feet of the <s>Sun</s>, the sages, and the teacher, this
<s>śāstra</s> has been compiled. Salutation to the earlier propounders!
